title: iodine DNS wire decoding
description: Parses bounded DNS questions, compressed names and actual answer records, then decodes iodine carrier bytes with the selected alphabet. Exact question identity and ordered answer pieces feed session correlation; a compact zlib header check supplies compressed framing evidence.

topics.title: Export shared iodine wire settings
topics.description: module Iodine shares the entry and state namespace. export makes the following typed constants available to local configuration through Iodine:: names.

ranges.code:
module Iodine;
export {

topics.title: Set independent persistent pool limits
topics.description: pending_limit defaults to 1024, candidate_limit to 256 and session_limit to 256. Each count has &redef. The state module applies these separate capacities when retaining DNS transactions, negotiation candidates and sessions.

topics.title: Set candidate, pending and session lifetimes
topics.description: The interval constants default candidate and pending retention to 30secs and session idle retention to 300secs. &redef exposes each lifetime to local configuration. State expiry compares these intervals with retained packet times.

topics.title: Bound expanded names, records and pointer jumps
topics.description: The defaults admit expanded DNS names through 255 bytes, at most 16 records across answer, authority and additional sections, and at most 10 compression pointer jumps per name. &redef exposes each count. These guards bound name expansion and record traversal for an admitted datagram.

topics.title: Set the UDP datagram byte limit
topics.description: max_datagram_bytes defaults to 8192 and has &redef. The entry handler enforces this limit before Raw signature routing or DNS wire decoding, bounding the input byte string reaching these helpers.

ranges.code: const max_datagram_bytes: count = 8192 &redef;

topics.title: Set fragment metadata and sweep budgets
topics.description: bounded_fragment_slots_per_session defaults to 32 and sweep_interval_seconds to 1secs. The state module divides the fragment budget between upstream and downstream metadata and uses the interval for cleanup scheduling; the entry handler uses the same interval for its expiry deadline.

topics.title: Translate zero based slices to sub_bytes
topics.description: cut accepts a zero based byte offset o and length n. It returns an empty string when o exceeds the string or n exceeds the remaining bytes. The o+1 argument translates the accepted offset to sub_bytes, whose positions start at one. Checking o first keeps the remaining length subtraction within the string.

ranges.code:
function cut(s: string, o: count, n: count): string
{ if (o > |s| || n > |s|-o) return ""; return sub_bytes(s,o+1,n); }

topics.title: Read one unsigned octet
topics.description: oct selects one byte through cut and converts the byte string with bytestring_to_count. Parser callers establish the enclosing bounds before interpreting length, flag, alphabet or header fields.

ranges.code:
function oct(s: string, o: count): count
{ return bytestring_to_count(cut(s,o,1)); }

topics.title: Read a two byte wire integer
topics.description: u16 selects two consecutive bytes at a zero based offset and converts their network byte order value with bytestring_to_count. DNS IDs, counts, flags, types, classes, lengths and answer ranks use this helper.

ranges.code:
function u16(s: string, o: count): count
{ return bytestring_to_count(cut(s,o,2)); }

topics.title: Construct an octet from its numeric value
topics.description: chr formats n as a hexadecimal string with %02x and converts it with hexstr_to_bytestring. Decoder output octets, DNS label lengths and extended alphabet bytes use this representation.

ranges.code: function chr(n: count): string { return hexstr_to_bytestring(fmt("%02x",n)); }

topics.title: Define iodine Base32 symbol values
topics.description: b32 assigns values 0 through 31 in the exact order abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345. Both Base32 decoding and single symbol command fields use this iodine alphabet.

ranges.code: const b32 = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345";

topics.title: Define iodine Base64 and Base64u symbol order
topics.description: b64 uses `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ-0123456789+` in that exact order. b64u uses the same ordering with _ as its final symbol. The decoder assigns six bits to each symbol and preserves case for these alphabets.

ranges.code:
const b64 = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ-0123456789+";
const b64u = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ-0123456789_";

topics.title: Start the byte oriented Base128 alphabet
topics.description: b128 begins with lowercase letters, uppercase letters and digits, in that order. The initialization handler appends byte values 188 through 253 to complete the 128 symbol alphabet.

ranges.code: global b128 = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789";

topics.title: Return decoded bytes with explicit validity
topics.description: Decoded defaults ok to F and data and codec to empty strings. Successful decoding returns ok=T with the local output bytes and exact codec name. Returning [] uses these failure defaults.

ranges.code: type Decoded: record { ok: bool &default=F; data: string &default=""; codec: string &default=""; };

topics.title: Convert a single case folded Base32 symbol
topics.description: b32val lowercases its input and searches b32 with find_str. A missing symbol or an input length other than one returns the sentinel 99. A valid symbol becomes its zero based count value through int_to_count.

ranges.code:
function b32val(s: string): count
{ local i=find_str(b32,to_lower(s)); if (i<0 || |s|!=1) return 99; return int_to_count(i); }

topics.title: Pass Raw carrier bytes through directly
topics.description: decode returns Raw input as data with ok=T and codec=Raw. This branch preserves the carrier bytes directly; the remaining branches select a symbol alphabet and build decoded bytes.

topics.title: Select codec width and reject unknown names
topics.description: Base32 begins with b32 and five bits per symbol. Base64 and Base64u select their respective alphabets and six bits. Base128 selects b128 and seven bits. Any other codec name returns the default invalid Decoded record.

topics.title: Allocate local decoding state
topics.description: acc, bits, out and i belong to this decode call. scale starts at 32, becomes 64 for six bit symbols or 128 for seven bit symbols. The loop visits the encoded string once, accumulating output in a local string that the caller receives with the decoded result.

topics.title: Validate and accumulate each encoded symbol
topics.description: The decoder reads one byte, folds case only for Base32 and finds its position in the selected alphabet. A missing symbol returns an invalid result immediately. Multiplication by scale shifts the retained bits, the symbol index adds the new value, and bits advances by the codec width.

topics.title: Emit complete bytes and retain residual bits
topics.description: When at least eight bits are available, the decoder subtracts eight from bits and builds 2 raised to that remaining count as divisor. acc/divisor supplies one output octet through chr; acc%divisor retains the residual low bits. Advancing i processes the next encoded byte.

topics.title: Return complete decoded bytes and codec
topics.description: The result marks decoding successful after all symbols pass their alphabet checks. data contains the complete output bytes accumulated in out; any final partial octet remains outside data. codec records the selected name for later carrier consistency checks.

ranges.code:
return [$ok=T,$data=out,$codec=codec];
}

links: Require one codec across answer pieces

topics.title: Represent expanded name bytes and encoded end
topics.description: Name defaults to invalid with end zero, empty labels and empty raw. A valid name returns literal label bytes, an expanded length prefixed raw form ending in a root byte, and end for the original encoded name’s next field.

ranges.code: type Name: record { ok: bool &default=F; end: count &default=0; labels: vector of string &default=vector(); raw: string &default=""; };

links: Return the expanded name and encoded end

topics.title: Initialize bounded name traversal
topics.description: name starts at the supplied zero based offset. pos follows labels or compression pointers; stop retains the original encoded end. jumps and seen track traversal, labels and raw build the expanded name, and expanded starts at one to reserve the terminating root byte.

topics.title: Reject a repeated name parse position
topics.description: Each loop checks pos against the local seen set before reading its octet, then records the position. Revisiting a label or pointer position returns an invalid Name, terminating cyclic compression paths.

ranges.code:
if (pos in seen) return []; add seen[pos];
local n=oct(s,pos);

links: Apply the separate pointer jump cap

topics.title: Follow compression pointers with a jump cap
topics.description: An octet at least 192 selects a two byte compression pointer. The guard requires both bytes and available jump budget. The first pointer fixes stop at pos+2; its low six bits and the next octet form the target offset. Incrementing jumps and next resumes traversal at that target. The loop bounds also reject targets outside the message.

topics.title: Finish at the root and preserve the encoded end
topics.description: The parser advances past the length octet. A zero octet finishes the name, using this position as stop for an uncompressed name or retaining the first pointer end. The returned raw string appends the root byte to expanded labels, so compression layout resolves to the same expanded representation.

ranges.code:
++pos;
if (n==0) { if (stop==0) stop=pos; return [$ok=T,$end=stop,$labels=labels,$raw=raw+"\x00"]; }

links: Build question identity from expanded bytes

topics.title: Validate label length, bounds and expanded size
topics.description: The guard admits label lengths through 63, requires all label bytes inside s and requires expanded+n+1 at most max_dns_name_bytes. The reserved root byte is already included in expanded. Values 64 through 191 reject here, while pointer octets use their own branch.

ranges.code: if (n>63 || pos+n>|s| || expanded+n+1>max_dns_name_bytes) return [];

links: Read the default 255 byte name cap

topics.title: Append literal label bytes or reject exhaustion
topics.description: The parser appends the label to labels, adds its length octet and contents to raw, and advances both expanded and pos. Falling out of the message before a terminating root returns an invalid Name. Literal label case remains in both expanded outputs.

topics.title: Join an exclusive range of labels
topics.description: joinlabels copies labels from first through last exclusive, placing sep only between entries. Callers choose an empty separator for encoded carrier chunks or a dot separator for a domain suffix. The caller supplies the label range.

topics.title: Read the carrier marker byte
topics.description: marked requires at least one byte, lowercases the first byte into mark and starts codec empty. host selects the hostname marker family; text carriers select the other family. Payload bytes retain their original case for the decoder.

topics.title: Map hostname carrier markers to codecs
topics.description: With host true, h selects Base32, i selects Base64, j selects Base64u and k selects Base128. These markers prefix the concatenated encoded labels of a CNAME, MX or SRV target.

topics.title: Map text carrier markers to codecs
topics.description: The text family maps t to Base32, s to Base64, u to Base64u, v to Base128 and r to Raw. The DNS TXT branch joins its character strings before applying this marker map.

topics.title: Remove the marker and decode the remaining bytes
topics.description: cut starts at offset one and selects the remaining |s|-1 bytes, removing exactly the marker byte. decode applies the selected codec; an unrecognized marker leaves codec empty and reaches decode’s invalid codec return.

ranges.code:
return decode(cut(s,1,|s|-1),codec);
}

links: Select the codec or return invalid

topics.title: Carry DNS identity and an optional decoded answer
topics.description: DNSWire stores validity, reply role, ID, type, class, question labels and serialized question bytes. answer defaults to an invalid Decoded record. An accepted envelope can therefore carry question metadata while its answer field remains invalid until a complete supported carrier qualifies.

topics.title: Require one complete standard DNS question
topics.description: dnswire requires a 12 byte header and QDCOUNT equal to one. It reads flags at offset two, requires opcode zero, RCODE zero and TC clear. These checks admit a standard successful, complete DNS envelope before expanding names or walking records.

topics.title: Cap records across all three DNS sections
topics.description: an, ns and ar read answer, authority and additional record counts from offsets 6, 8 and 10. Their sum must fit max_dns_records, whose default is 16. The later loop visits this bounded total while answer extraction uses the answer section prefix only.

ranges.code:
local an=u16(s,6); local ns=u16(s,8); local ar=u16(s,10);
if (an+ns+ar>max_dns_records) return [];

topics.title: Expand the question and require type and class bytes
topics.description: name begins at DNS offset 12. The parser requires a valid expanded name and four bytes after its original encoded end for QTYPE and QCLASS. This uses Name.end so compressed encoding and expanded identity remain separate.

ranges.code: local q=name(s,12); if (!q$ok || q$end+4>|s|) return [];

links: Read encoded end and expanded name

topics.title: Admit the seven iodine DNS question types
topics.description: qt and qc read the two byte type and class. Class must be IN, value 1. Supported types are A 1, CNAME 5, NULL 10, MX 15, TXT 16, SRV 33 and PRIVATE 65399. The actual answer type later selects the matching carrier wrapper, including CNAME for an A question.

ranges.code:
local qt=u16(s,q$end); local qc=u16(s,q$end+2);
if (qc!=1 || qt !in set(1,5,10,15,16,33,65399)) return [];

links: Select CNAME, MX and SRV wrappers

topics.title: Initialize a bounded record walk and local pieces
topics.description: pos begins after QTYPE and QCLASS, and idx counts the declared records. parts, piececodec, valid and found are local to this datagram parse. The loop visits the bounded sum of all three sections, retaining decoded carrier pieces only for qualifying answer records.

topics.title: Bound each resource record header and RDATA
topics.description: The owner name must expand successfully and leave ten bytes for the fixed RR header. The parser reads type, class and RDLENGTH, advances over that header and requires all n RDATA bytes inside the message. Owner name pointers receive the same cycle, jump and expanded size guards as question names.

topics.title: Require answer section, IN class and exact owner
topics.description: idx<an selects the actual answer section. cls==1 requires IN and owner$raw==q$raw requires exact expanded question owner bytes, including label case and root. Only this branch attempts carrier decoding. Each candidate begins with invalid d and rank 10.

ranges.code:
if (idx<an && cls==1 && owner$raw==q$raw) {
local d: Decoded=[]; local rank: count=10;

topics.title: Read raw bytes from NULL or PRIVATE answers
topics.description: A NULL question with NULL answer, or PRIVATE 65399 question with the same answer type, passes all n RDATA bytes to decode as Raw. The enclosing answer owner and class guard supplies the record identity.

ranges.code: if ((qt==10 || qt==65399) && typ==qt) d=decode(cut(s,pos,n),"Raw");

topics.title: Join bounded TXT character strings and decode a marker
topics.description: A TXT question requires a TXT answer. The loop reads each one byte string length, advances j and requires that string to fit the remaining RDATA. It concatenates the exact string bytes in text, then marked(text,F) selects the text marker family and decodes the payload.

topics.title: Select actual CNAME, MX or SRV target framing
topics.description: A or CNAME questions accept an actual CNAME answer. MX questions require MX answers and SRV questions require SRV answers. skip is zero for CNAME, two bytes for MX preference and six bytes for SRV priority, weight and port. RDATA must contain bytes after those fixed fields for its target name.

topics.title: Read wrapper rank and validate the entire target name
topics.description: MX and SRV use their first two RDATA bytes as rank; CNAME retains rank 10. The target name starts after skip and must end exactly at pos+n. It must contain at least two labels with an exact two byte final label. Compression expansion uses the same bounded name parser.

topics.title: Join payload labels and apply hostname markers
topics.description: joinlabels concatenates every target label before the final two byte label with an empty separator. marked(...,T) reads the hostname codec marker and decodes the remaining symbols. The final label serves as a wrapper and stays outside the encoded payload.

ranges.code:
d=marked(joinlabels(target$labels,0,|target$labels|-1,""),T);
}

topics.title: Validate answer piece ranks before assembly
topics.description: Only d$ok results contribute pieces. A rank of zero, a rank outside multiples of ten, a rank above ten times max_dns_records or a repeated rank sets valid=F. The data is stored by rank even on that path, and final answer qualification requires valid to remain true.

topics.title: Require the same codec across decoded pieces
topics.description: Once a piece has been found, every later decoded piece must have the same codec as piececodec. A mismatch clears valid. The parser records the current codec and sets found, retaining only this datagram’s local piece table and codec state for assembly.
links: Read the exact decoder codec name

topics.title: Advance over each declared RDATA region
topics.description: After carrier processing, pos advances by the declared RDATA length and idx advances by one. Authority and additional records receive structural traversal through this same loop; the answer section guard selects the records that contribute payload pieces.

ranges.code:
pos+=n; ++idx;
}

links: Read the section and owner selector

topics.title: Require exact message consumption
topics.description: pos must equal the datagram length after every declared record has been traversed. Trailing bytes or an inconsistent section layout return an invalid DNSWire. The local answer starts as invalid before the assembly guard.

ranges.code:
if (pos!=|s|) return [];
local answer: Decoded=[];

topics.title: Assemble consecutive ranks beginning at ten
topics.description: Assembly requires at least one decoded piece and valid=T. Starting at rank 10, the loop concatenates pieces at 10, 20 and subsequent increments of ten. The final count check requires every stored piece to belong to that contiguous sequence. A successful result returns the combined bytes and shared codec.

topics.title: Return exact expanded question identity and DNS role
topics.description: The result marks the envelope valid, derives reply from the DNS QR bit through flags>=32768 and returns the wire ID, type, class and expanded labels. question concatenates q$raw with the exact QTYPE and QCLASS bytes. This normalizes compression layout into an expanded length prefixed identity while preserving label bytes and case. The state module hashes this identity in pkey alongside peers, ports and DNS ID.

ranges.code:
return [$ok=T,$reply=flags>=32768,$id=u16(s,0),$qtype=qt,$qclass=qc,$labels=q$labels,$question=q$raw+cut(s,q$end,4),$answer=answer];
}

topics.title: Require two header bytes and a bounded body minimum
topics.description: zheader receives header bytes s and a separate total body length. It requires at least two available bytes and length at least eight, then reads the two header octets. Fragment processing can pass its retained two byte prefix together with the summed fragment lengths.

topics.title: Validate the zlib method, window and header checksum
topics.description: The first octet must select compression method 8 in its low nibble and a window size field through 7 in its high nibble. The combined two byte header must be divisible by 31 and the preset dictionary flag must be clear. These fixed header tests supply compressed framing evidence using the prefix and total length.
links: Read the prefix and length inputs

topics.title: Complete Base128 before packet processing
topics.description: zeek_init at priority 20 appends byte values 188 through 253 inclusive using chr. Combined with the 62 initial letter and digit symbols, this forms the 128 symbol byte alphabet used by Base128 decoding. Priority 20 runs before the entry module’s priority 10 port initialization.

ranges.code:
event zeek_init() &priority=20
{ local i: count=188; while (i<=253) { b128+=chr(i); ++i; } }
